//: Emit config for the stdio entry. The sibling tsconfig.json is noEmit:true — a
typecheck-only config — so there was no build output at all before this.
Why emit exists (2026-07-31): every claude-code turn tears down its Worker and
respawns the stdio MCP children, and each child pays tsx compiling stdio.ts's
whole module graph. Measured on this box: plain node ~70ms, node --import tsx
~218ms, node --import tsx + stdio.ts ~1195ms — and the evolve chain pays it
TWICE (bridge + child), so ~2s of every turn is spent recompiling an unchanged
file. That is the window in which a fresh worker's first tool call arrives
before tools/list has registered: 53 'No such tool available: mcp__ar-tools__*'
misses in one cartridge log, 50 of which recovered on a later call.
Consuming this build is GATED ON MTIME at spawn (container-manager.ts): dist is
used only when newer than the newest src input, else the tsx path runs. Nothing
in the tree checks this output's currency — packages/tools is not a `file:`
target of any cartridge, so rebuild-all's discovery never reaches it, and
check-stale only tests existence. The mtime gate is therefore the ONLY guard,
and it is what keeps a stale build from silently serving every agent's file and
shell tools. Worst case is the cost we already pay.
